{{short description|Statistical test}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Box's ''M'' test}}
'''Box's ''M'' test''' is a multivariate statistical test used to check the equality of multiple [[variance-covariance matrix|variance-covariance matrices]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Box |first1=G.E.P. |title=A General Distribution Theory for a Class of Likelihood Criteria |journal=Biometrika |date=1 December 1949 |volume=36 |issue=3-4 |pages=317–346 |doi=10.1093/biomet/36.3-4.317}}</ref> The test is commonly used to test the assumption of [[homogeneity]] of variances and covariances in [[MANOVA]] and [[linear discriminant analysis]]. It is named after [[George E. P. Box]], who first discussed the test in 1949. The test uses a [[chi-squared distribution|chi-squared]] approximation.

Box's ''M'' test is susceptible to errors if the data does not meet model assumptions or if the sample size is too large or small.<ref name="Warner2013">{{cite book|author=Rebecca M. Warner|title=Applied Statistics: From Bivariate Through Multivariate Techniques|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=b1bXhepuJOEC&pg=PT778|year=2013|publisher=SAGE|isbn=978-1-4129-9134-6|pages=778}}</ref> Box's ''M'' test is especially prone to error if the data does not meet the assumption of [[multivariate normal]]ity.<ref name="Manly2004">{{cite book|author=Bryan F.J. Manly|title=Multivariate Statistical Methods: A Primer, Third Edition|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bLSEeMjvD9oC&pg=PA54|date=6 July 2004|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-58488-414-9|pages=54}}</ref>
